newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HSBC Holdings soars to another record close.
newsitem.headline: HSBC Holdings soars to another record close.

text.p: Shares of international banking giant HSBC Holdings Plc set a new closing high in Hong Kong for the third day in a row on Tuesday, propelled higher by Wall Street and a positive earnings outlook, analysts said.
"HSBC is a top performer and deserves to be. It is certainly going to perform as well as the index," Alan Hutcheson, director of research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

The share rose HK$3.00, or 1.5 percent, to close at HK$205.00 after retreating from an intra-day high of HK$207. It topped topped the most active list with 3.71 million shares worth HK$762.84 million changing hands.
The Hang Seng Index rose 181.38 points, or 1.35 percent, to finish at 13,580.72 on Tuesday, prompted by the strong performance of the Dow Jones Industrial index overnight.

The Dow soared 143.29 points, or 2.03 percent, to 7,214.49 on growing expectations of a cut in the U.S. capital gains tax and a belief that inflation in the U.S. will be kept in check despite the strong U.S. economy.
"A lot of people still think HSBC is going to produce solid growth. Also the U.S. and the European markets are setting record highs," said Percy Au-Young, director of research at DBS Securities.
"Banks are doing very well in those markets and HSBC is an international bank."
Analysts said HSBC had a favourable outlook in Hong Kong with its growing economy, and benefits from a positive global environment with steady growth and low inflation pressure.

The bank, which was trading at about 13 times 1997 earnings, was still cheap when compared with the ratio of 18 for its local subsidiary Hang Seng Bank Ltd, said Henry Lui, an analyst at Mansion House Research.
HSBC Holdings has risen about 24 percent so far this year while the blue chip barometer Hang Seng Index has climbed only 0.95 percent.
But Deutsche Morgan's Hutcheson said he doubted that the stock would continue to outperform the main index.
"The index overall is pretty much flat - up slightly from the start of the year - but you are talking about a stock that is up 24 percent already this year," he said.
"I would be reluctant to say it is going to be a huge winner like that from this point," he added.
Other analysts also said HSBC Holdings should move in line with the market with a correction possible when this current rally loses steam.
"In the past few years, after a major price rally HSBC would correct, triming about one-third off any gains and I bet this patten would continue," Mansion House's Lui said.

HSBC Holding's average P/E in the past few years was slightly above 10 times and it looked expensive at the current price level, said Steven Thompson an analyst at Nikko Research Centre (Hong Kong) Ltd.
"There is a tendency for share prices to return to the average in the long term," he said.
Despite its recent gains and the need for a near-term correction, analysts remain bullish on the longer term outlook for the share, forecasting a year end target of between HK$220 and HK$250 in 1997.
That would put the the Hang Seng Index at 15,000 by the end of December, they said.
